remarks.p: Consumers of this file should refer to the Essentials OSCAL NS 1.0 page for information regarding the Essentials specific representation used in this OSCAL file.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data) are continually and centrally identified and documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Maintain current records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets.

part.name: item
part.p: A maintained record of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets has not been established.

part.name: item
part.p: There is no defined process for identifying, recording, reviewing and updating asset records.

part.name: item
part.p: Asset records are maintained, but identified omissions, inaccuracies or newly discovered assets are not triaged and addressed within the timeframes or tolerances defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A process to update the asset inventory runs on a schedule but the results are not reconciled or updated within a period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: At each scheduled review or update, records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets are complete and accurate within the tolerances defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A defined process identifies changes and newly discovered assets between scheduled reviews, and ensures that records are reviewed, reconciled and updated within timeframes commensurate with the associated cyber security risk.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are planned, designed, developed, tested, deployed, maintained and decommissioned according to their business criticality ratings and security and resilience requirements using Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

part.name: statement
part.p: Design systems securely to provide visibility, enforce authorised access, protect data, minimise required and default privileges, limit exposed services and remove unnecessary functionality.

part.name: item
part.p: Systems are deployed with default configurations and no evidence of security design considerations.

part.name: item
part.p: Unnecessary services, protocols or functionality remain enabled with no documented rationale.

part.name: item
part.p: Security telemetry is not enabled or is not considered as part of system design.

part.name: item
part.p: Security is considered during system design but not consistently applied across all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Some unnecessary services have been disabled but a systematic review has not been completed.

part.name: item
part.p: Security telemetry is partially enabled but gaps in coverage exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Systems are designed and deployed with exposed services limited, required and default permissions minimised, data protections in place, authorised access enforced, and only required functionality enabled.

part.name: item
part.p: Security telemetry is enabled by default.

part.name: item
part.p: Evidence exists that security design decisions are recorded and reviewed during system changes.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secure build and deployment processes to enforce controls consistently across systems.

part.name: item
part.p: No controlled build or deployment process exists for applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Changes to systems are applied ad hoc, without any version control, testing or approval.

part.name: item
part.p: A controlled deployment process exists but is not consistently followed for all changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Version control is in place but pre-deployment security verification is not performed.

part.name: item
part.p: A controlled build and deployment process is in place and consistently followed.

part.name: item
part.p: Configuration changes are subject to version control, testing and approval before deployment.

part.name: item
part.p: Security controls are confirmed to be implemented consistently across systems following deployment processes.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber supply chains supporting systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are secure, resilient and support effective and coordinated cyber security incident response.

part.name: statement
part.p: Assess the integrity and authenticity of software, components and updates before use, and verify provenance where suitable supplier evidence is available.

part.name: item
part.p: No verification of software, component or update integrity or authenticity is performed before introduction into systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification outcomes are not recorded or available for review.

part.name: item
part.p: Where verification cannot be performed, no compensating control or remediation paths are documented.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification is performed for some categories of software but not consistently across operating systems, applications, firmware and dependencies.

part.name: item
part.p: Integrity or provenance checks are performed, but they do not provide sufficient assurance for all software, components or updates.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification outcomes are recorded for some software, components or updates prior to being introduced into systems, but not consistently.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls exist for some unverifiable components but are not formally approved or time-bound.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification of integrity and provenance is performed for software, components and updates across all relevant categories, and provenance is verified where suitable supplier evidence is available.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification uses one or more mechanisms appropriate to the software, component, update and source to provide reliable assurance of integrity and provenance.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification outcomes are recorded and available for review.

part.name: item
part.p: Where verification cannot be performed, compensating controls are applied, exceptions are time-bound and remediation paths are documented.

group.title: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management

part.name: overview
part.p: Robust and secure identity, credential and access management is used to establish, maintain and control access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) and to support effective detection of identity and credential misuse.

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify and disable or remove default and unused accounts regularly, permitting exceptions only where the account is documented, justified, hardened and monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: No review of default or unused accounts has been conducted within the review period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Default vendor accounts remain enabled on production systems without appropriate documentation, justification, hardening and monitoring in place for their use.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to identify accounts that have not authenticated within a defined period.

part.name: item
part.p: A review has been conducted but does not cover all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Default accounts have been identified but some remain enabled without documented justification.

part.name: item
part.p: Unused accounts are identified but remediation is incomplete or delayed beyond defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: A review of accounts has been completed within the defined review period covering all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Default accounts are disabled or have approved justification for remaining active, with appropriate monitoring and compensating controls for their use in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Accounts that show no evidence of use, other than approved emergency access accounts, are identified and either disabled or removed in accordance with defined timeframes.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation

part.name: statement
part.p: Use phishing-resistant MFA for users authenticating to systems, including from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is not enforced for interactive user authentication to systems.

part.name: item
part.p: MFA is deployed but uses non-phishing-resistant methods, such as SMS, voice, or push-only authentication instead of phishing-resistant MFA.

part.name: item
part.p: No access policies differentiate between trusted and untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Access from untrusted, external or high-risk locations is permitted without MFA, or with non-phishing-resistant MFA.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is deployed for some but not all systems within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Access policies exist but do not cover all organisationally defined high-risk location categories.

part.name: item
part.p: Exceptions or alternative authentication pathways allow routine or recurring authentication without phishing-resistant MFA, or emergency access arrangements are not adequately restricted, monitored, tested or reviewed.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for all routine interactive user authentication to systems within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for routine authentication attempts from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Customer-facing services provide a phishing-resistant MFA option for authentication.

part.name: item
part.p: Emergency access arrangements are periodically tested and reviewed to confirm that they remain operational, appropriately protected and limited to their intended purpose. Credentials or authentication factors used for emergency access are securely managed and are not used for routine administration.

part.name: statement
part.p: Disable legacy authentication protocols or, where this is not feasible, restrict and monitor their use, apply compensating controls and establish a time-bound decommissioning plan.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce modern authentication controls remain enabled and in active use without restriction.

part.name: item
part.p: No assessment has been conducted to identify which legacy authentication protocols are in use within the environment.

part.name: item
part.p: Authentication mechanisms transmitting credentials in cleartext or using weak cryptographic primitives remain enabled and no action has been taken to disable them.

part.name: item
part.p: Where legacy protocols are retained, no compensating controls, no monitoring and no decommissioning timelines are in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy authentication protocols have been identified and are partially restricted but some remain enabled across systems within scope without justification.

part.name: item
part.p: An assessment has been conducted but does not cover all in-scope systems, or the inventory of legacy protocols in use is not maintained.

part.name: item
part.p: Some weak authentication mechanisms have been disabled but others remain enabled without documented justification or remediation plan.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls exist for some retained legacy protocols but monitoring is inconsistent or decommissioning timelines are not defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce modern authentication controls have been identified and disabled across systems within scope, excluding documented and risk accepted exceptions.

part.name: item
part.p: An assessment of legacy authentication protocol use has been conducted across in-scope systems and the inventory is maintained.

part.name: item
part.p: Where retention is necessary, compensating controls are applied and decommissioning timelines are recorded and tracked.

part.name: item
part.p: Ongoing use of legacy authentication protocols is regularly risk reviewed, accepted and recorded in the organisation’s risk register.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ensure that user, machine, system and service account credentials are unique per system or account, particularly in high-privilege contexts.

part.name: item
part.p: Local administrator credentials are shared across the device fleet, or service or privileged account credentials are routinely reused across systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness is not enforced for applicable user, machine, system or service identities.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness has not been addressed in high-privilege contexts, including domain administration, cloud administration or automation platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Where credential uniqueness cannot be enforced, neither compensating controls nor remediation paths are in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Local administrator credential uniqueness has been implemented for some device populations but coverage is incomplete across the device fleet.

part.name: item
part.p: A technical mechanism is in place but applies to only a subset of credential types or systems within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness has been addressed in some high-privilege contexts but gaps remain in others.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls exist for some shared credentials but monitoring is inconsistent or remediation plans do not exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Credentials for applicable local administrative accounts are unique to each system or account.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness is consistently enforced for applicable user, machine, system and service identities.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness is enforced consistently in high-privilege contexts, with managed identities or equivalent capabilities used in preference to shared static credentials wherever feasible.

part.name: item
part.p: Where uniqueness cannot be enforced, compensating controls are applied, the use of the shared credentials is monitored, and a remediation plan exists.

part.name: overview
part.p: Users are granted the minimum access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) required to undertake their duties or functions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Periodically review and update access privileges in alignment with current roles, duties and business requirements.

part.name: item
part.p: Access privileges are not reviewed against current roles, duties and business requirements.

part.name: item
part.p: Access reviews do not identify privileges that are no longer required.

part.name: item
part.p: Access privileges are not updated when personnel roles, duties or business requirements change.

part.name: item
part.p: Access privileges are not mapped to roles, duties and business requirements.

part.name: item
part.p: Access reviews are conducted for some accounts or systems, but coverage is incomplete.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews identify excessive or obsolete privileges, but updates are incomplete or not completed within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A process to review access privileges exists but only occurs on an ad hoc basis.

part.name: item
part.p: Some access privileges are mapped to roles, duties and business requirements, but not all.

part.name: item
part.p: Access privileges for all applicable accounts and systems are reviewed within a cycle defined by the organisation and aligned with current roles, duties and business requirements.

part.name: item
part.p: Privileges identified as excessive or obsolete are removed or updated within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Review outcomes and resulting access changes are documented and available as evidence.

part.name: item
part.p: Access privileges are mapped to current roles, duties and business requirements.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are securely configured to approved and maintained baselines, including by reducing attack surfaces and attack paths, with configurations continually monitored and consistently enforced.

part.name: statement
part.p: Define approved configuration baselines, informed by vendor and industry hardening guidance, that disable or remove unnecessary services, insecure settings, and unsupported or weak communication protocols.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented configuration baseline exists for assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Systems are deployed with vendor defaults and no documented hardening has been applied.

part.name: item
part.p: A baseline exists but does not address all applicable asset types.

part.name: item
part.p: The baseline is documented but has not been reviewed or updated within the cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: The baseline exists but rationale for configuration decisions is not documented.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented and approved baseline exists for all applicable asset types.

part.name: item
part.p: The baseline disables or removes unnecessary services, insecure settings, and unsupported or weak communication protocols.

part.name: item
part.p: Configuration decisions are documented with rationale to support drift assessment.

part.name: item
part.p: The baseline is reviewed and updated on a cycle defined by the organisation.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Command and Scripting Interpreter

part.name: statement
part.p: Deploy approved configuration baselines on systems, including infrastructure, operating systems and applications.

part.name: item
part.p: Approved baselines have not been applied to assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Baseline deployment has not been validated through technical assessment.

part.name: item
part.p: Approved baselines have been implemented where available, but some relevant asset types are not covered by an approved baseline.

part.name: item
part.p: Deployment has occurred but validation through technical assessment is incomplete or not current.

part.name: item
part.p: Approved baselines have been deployed, but coverage for all applicable assets is inconsistent.

part.name: item
part.p: Approved baselines have been applied to all applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Deployment has been validated through technical assessment.

part.name: item
part.p: Coverage metrics are available demonstrating deployment completeness.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Detect and respond to configuration drift using scheduled technical assessments and, where supported, automated monitoring, based on system criticality and change rate.

part.name: item
part.p: No mechanism exists to detect configuration drift from approved baselines.

part.name: item
part.p: Assessments to detect configuration drift have not been conducted within the review period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Assessments do not systematically identify instances of configuration drift for assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Drift detection is in place but does not cover all applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Drift is detected but the remediation process is informal or response timeframes are not defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Automated configuration monitoring or regular technical assessments detect drift across the applicable assets, occurring at a frequency based on system criticality and change rate.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented remediation process exists with defined response timeframes aligned to severity.

part.name: item
part.p: Drift events are tracked to closure with evidence of remediation.

part.name: overview
part.p: Vulnerabilities in systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified, documented, validated and prioritised for remediation or mitigation in a timely manner, with all remediation and mitigation actions verified for effectiveness.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Mitigated technique: Exploitation of Remote Services
Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Client Execution

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify known software and configuration weaknesses of assets through continuous and repeatable assessment activities, including vulnerability scanning activities.

part.name: item
part.p: Vulnerability scanning activities are not undertaken.

part.name: item
part.p: No routine vulnerability assessment activity has been conducted within a period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Advisories for relevant software and configuration weaknesses for organisational assets are not reviewed and assessed for impact.

part.name: item
part.p: Vulnerability scanning is deployed but does not cover all applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Vulnerability scans are conducted but results are not reviewed and prioritised within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Vulnerability scans are conducted but frequency is not regular enough to enable timely response.

part.name: item
part.p: Scanning covers software vulnerabilities but not configuration weaknesses.

part.name: item
part.p: Advisories for relevant software and configuration weaknesses for organisational assets are reviewed on an ad hoc basis, or only for some assets.

part.name: item
part.p: All applicable assets are included in routine vulnerability scanning, and scanning frequency enables timely response.

part.name: item
part.p: Scanning covers both software vulnerabilities and configuration weaknesses.

part.name: item
part.p: Results are reviewed and prioritised within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Advisories for relevant software and configuration weaknesses in all organisational assets are regularly reviewed and assessed for impact.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Mitigated technique: Exploitation of Remote Services
Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Client Execution

part.name: statement
part.p: Apply security patches or updates within defined risk-based timeframes or automatically where operational impact is low.

part.name: item
part.p: No defined patching timeframes exist for applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Patches are not applied or are applied on an ad hoc basis with no tracking.

part.name: item
part.p: Expected patching timeframes are defined by the organisation but are not consistently met.

part.name: item
part.p: Patches are applied but compensating controls are not documented where operational constraints prevent timely patching.

part.name: item
part.p: Patching coverage metrics exist but show significant gaps.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk-based patching timeframes defined by the organisation are in place and consistently met.

part.name: item
part.p: Patching is prioritised based on vulnerability severity, exposure and exploit availability.

part.name: item
part.p: Where operational constraints prevent timely patching, compensating controls are documented and approved.

part.name: item
part.p: Patching coverage metrics account for all applicable assets, with any exclusions identified and formally risk accepted.

part.name: item
part.p: Automatic patching of assets is applied where available and the organisation has determined operational impact is low.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Mitigated technique: Exploitation of Remote Services
Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Client Execution

part.name: statement
part.p: Remediate or mitigate vulnerabilities exceeding defined risk thresholds within defined timeframes based on exploitation, exposure, criticality, impact and compensating controls, and verify treatment effectiveness.

part.name: item
part.p: No risk thresholds are defined for vulnerability remediation.

part.name: item
part.p: Vulnerabilities exceeding acceptable risk levels are not tracked or remediated.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk thresholds are defined but vulnerabilities exceeding them are not consistently remediated within defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls are applied in some cases but are not formally documented or approved.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk thresholds defined by the organisation exist, and vulnerabilities exceeding them are remediated or have approved compensating controls within organisationally defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: Remediation and mitigation actions are tracked to closure with verification that actions reduced the risk as intended.

part.name: item
part.p: The process is sustained, with historical data demonstrating consistent performance across organisationally defined reporting periods.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (operating systems and applications) only permit the execution of software that is supported, verified and authorised.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools
Mitigated technique: Command and Scripting Interpreter
Mitigated technique: System Binary Proxy Execution

part.name: statement
part.p: Permit only supported, verified and organisation-authorised software to execute on systems, with exceptions minimised, formally risk accepted, time-bound, monitored and regularly reviewed.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsupported, unverified or unauthorised software can execute without restriction.

part.name: item
part.p: The list of approved software does not exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Execution restriction controls are deployed but do not cover all applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: The organisation maintains a list of approved software, but it has not been reviewed within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Execution restrictions are in place but integrity verification of approved software is not performed.

part.name: item
part.p: Exceptions to execution restrictions are granted without formal approval or time-bounding.

part.name: item
part.p: Controls restrict execution to supported, organisation-authorised and integrity-verified software on all applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: The organisation maintains a list of approved software and reviews it within the timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Integrity of permitted software is verified using trusted mechanisms appropriate to the software and its source.

part.name: item
part.p: Exceptions are formally approved, documented, time-bound and reviewed on a regular cycle defined by the organisation.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools
Mitigated technique: Command and Scripting Interpreter
Mitigated technique: System Binary Proxy Execution

part.name: statement
part.p: Restrict administrative and management tooling to approved software sets and executed from only authorised, known locations.

part.name: item
part.p: No approved administrative toolset is defined.

part.name: item
part.p: No restrictions are placed on the location administrative tooling can be executed from.

part.name: item
part.p: No controls prevent unapproved administrative tools, including tools commonly used in post-compromise activity, from executing on managed assets.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved toolset is defined but not consistently enforced across all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Administrative tooling is configured to execute from known locations, but privileged users can still run tooling from unapproved locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Some unapproved administrative tools are blocked but enforcement gaps exist.

part.name: item
part.p: A defined and enforced approved toolset exists for administrative and management activities, and execution is limited to authorised, known locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Administrative and management tooling outside the approved set is blocked from execution, including from unauthorised locations.

part.name: overview
part.p: Security-relevant event logs and configuration changes for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are centrally collected, protected against unauthorised modification or deletion, and retained to support effective cyber security event detection and investigation.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Protect event logs from unauthorised access, modification or deletion, including by encrypting them during transit and at rest and securing the systems and accounts used to store, manage and analyse them.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs generated by applicable assets are not protected from modification or deletion.

part.name: item
part.p: Log access is not restricted to authorised roles with a business need.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are neither encrypted during transit nor at rest.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are forwarded but integrity protections are not in place at the source.

part.name: item
part.p: Log access is restricted but some roles retain the ability to modify or delete logs.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are encrypted during transit but are not protected with encryption at rest (or vice versa).

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are protected against modification or deletion.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are encrypted in transit and at rest.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to logs is restricted to authorised roles with a business need.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Forward high-value, security-relevant event logs and configuration changes from infrastructure, operating systems and applications to a central log storage capability.

part.name: item
part.p: Security-relevant logs from assets are not forwarded to a central logging capability.

part.name: item
part.p: High-value, security-relevant event logs or configuration changes from infrastructure, operating systems or applications are not forwarded.

part.name: item
part.p: High-value, security-relevant event logs are forwarded, but coverage gaps are identified or completeness has not been validated.

part.name: item
part.p: Configuration change logs are forwarded inconsistently.

part.name: item
part.p: The utility of security log sources is reviewed, but on an ad hoc basis rather than according to a defined schedule.

part.name: item
part.p: Log forwarding is in place but latency is excessive for effective detection.

part.name: item
part.p: High-value security-relevant event logs and configuration changes from all relevant infrastructure, operating systems and application sources are forwarded to the central logging capability.

part.name: item
part.p: Security log sources are reviewed at regular intervals to ensure their continued utility in detecting and responding to changing adversary techniques.

part.name: item
part.p: Log completeness has been validated against the expected log sources.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are forwarded at a frequency that enables timely detection.

part.name: overview
part.p: Anomalous or unexpected events and behaviours for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ensure event logs are normalised, time-synchronised and enriched to support correlation across systems and environments.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are not time-synchronised to an authoritative source.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are ingested in raw format and are neither normalised nor enriched.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are time-synchronised but are not normalised to a common schema.

part.name: item
part.p: Some enrichment is applied but critical contextual data such as asset classification or account type is missing.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are time-synchronised to the authoritative time source.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are normalised into the common log schema and enriched with contextual metadata.

part.name: item
part.p: Enriched logs support correlation across relevant systems, environments and data sources in the central logging platform.
